description: Initial source-distributed byte splitting capability checkpoint; broad strings/bytes goal remains open
namespace_proposal: Data.Bytes.Split source-distributed; no new embedded-base dependencies
concrete_types: opaque ByteSplitFactory retains fixed input/separator endpoints, raw-vs-compiled separator policy, Option Nat limit and mode
opaque ByteSplitState carries immutable explicit producer position, emitted count and completion
opaque ByteSplitCursor owns private checked progress bytes and retains its factory; copied handles share progress without changing Producer semantics
invariants: all coordinates relative to a checked ByteView; outputs retain whole owner and share mutations
None limit is unlimited; Some0 yields nothing; Some1 returns unsplit remainder; last limited chunk retains all remaining bytes
nonempty-separator splitting preserves leading/trailing empty chunks; empty input yields one empty chunk
empty separator yields one bounded UTF8 sequence per chunk, malformed bytes advance one; empty input yields no chunks
line iteration includes LF and any preceding CR, preserves unterminated final line, omits extra empty chunk after trailing LF
pure Producer values carry explicit resumable state and can be folded afresh; do not claim mutable single-use iterator semantics
list collectors use a tail accumulator then tail reversal, not allocation during recursive unwinding
raw separator views retain live mutable contents and are read at each explicit step; explicitly named compiled variants alone snapshot separators
preserve Data.Producer explicit advance/replay semantics; fresh traversal factory and separately named pull cursor distinguish callback single-use behavior
backing_safety_proposal: Consumes checked byte-view-utf8-at from separately tested ByteView dependency; no backing or address access
fixture_plan: independent pinned SDK and Python complete chunk hex/digests for both list and sequence forms
empty/missing/overlap separators, all limit boundaries, invalid/truncated UTF8 views, NUL, CRLF, bare CR, LF tails
early producer stop via prod-take, complete fold and repeated fold, mutation between steps, fresh pattern stability and retained temporary owners
deep chunk lists O0/8MiB, bounded normal32MiB and per-assertion poison256MiB, zero leaks both frontends
public split/list/fold pipelines with existing SIMD/SWAR search kernels and assembly review

capability_mapping.Split: bytes-split / byte-view-split -> List ByteView retained aliases
capability_mapping.SplitAfter: bytes-split-after / byte-view-split-after -> List ByteView including separators
capability_mapping.SplitN: bytes-split-limit / byte-view-split-limit; None maps any negative/unlimited, Some Nat is concrete nonnegative maximum
capability_mapping.SplitAfterN: bytes-split-after-limit / byte-view-split-after-limit with the same explicit limit policy
capability_mapping.SplitSeq: bytes-split-seq / byte-view-split-seq -> persistent Producer ByteSplitState ByteView; explicit factory -> fresh byte-split-cursor maps shared single-use pull state
capability_mapping.SplitAfterSeq: bytes-split-after-seq / byte-view-split-after-seq with included delimiter aliases; same explicit cursor lifecycle
capability_mapping.Lines: bytes-lines / byte-view-lines -> concrete Producer; byte-view-lines-factory -> fresh cursor; LF included, CR preserved, trailingempty omitted

public_state_contract: Factory retains immutable endpoints/live raw owners. Producer carries immutable explicit progress and preserves replay. Separately named Cursor is sequential shared progress; copied handles share it, independent factories/cursors do not; close/exhaustion remains None.
errors_and_edge_policies: Negative limits cannot inhabit Nat: explicit None means unlimited; Some0 is empty and Some1 preserves the final unsplit remainder.
No numeric raw range API is introduced: callers provide sealed ByteView values whose construction returns existing checked range errors.
Raw bytes remain arbitrary, including NUL and malformed/truncated UTF8. Empty separator consumes one valid bounded sequence or one malformed byte.
Fixed compiled separator ownership is explicit. Raw input/separator mutations, including overlap with yielded fragments, remain observable between advances.
standalone_dependency: Relative UTF8 observation2691 and exact-byte query91c3 with parent actual wasm/ARM/PPC coverage; initial Split does not yet select the exact-byte optimization
